title: GraphQL Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Ask for one field
examples.description: A schema names allowed fields. The resolver supplies a value for greeting.

examples.title: Choose part of an object
examples.description: The query picks title and leaves out pages. The resolver still holds both fields.

examples.title: Give a field an input
examples.description: An argument supplies a value to a field. The resolver receives it in an object.

examples.title: Keep query text and values apart
examples.description: A variable lets one query be reused with different values. Its value is supplied separately.

examples.title: Read several objects
examples.description: Square brackets describe a list type. The query selects title for each book.

examples.title: Give results different names
examples.description: Aliases name two uses of the same field so both results can appear together.

examples.title: Reuse a field selection
examples.description: A fragment gives a group of fields a name. The query spreads that group onto a Book.

examples.title: Use a named set of choices
examples.description: An enum limits a value to named choices. GREEN is a schema label, not arbitrary text.

examples.title: Ask for a change
examples.description: A mutation names a write action. This local example changes one in-memory score.

examples.title: Require a value
examples.description: The exclamation mark means a field must not be null. This resolver breaks that rule, so GraphQL reports an error.
examples.output: Cannot return null for non-nullable field Query.name.

examples.title: Choose fields with a flag
examples.description: The include directive can choose whether a field is requested. The flag is false here.

examples.title: Group several inputs
examples.description: An input type groups values sent into a mutation. It is separate from an output object type.
